===== striped-block-deletion-safety =====
title: HDFS-16420. Avoid deleting unique data blocks when deleting redundancy striped blocks.
category: other
requirement: "HDFS-16420. Avoid deleting unique data blocks when deleting redundancy striped blocks.\n\n<!--\nThanks for sending a pull request!\n  1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/HADOOP/How+To+Contribute\n  2. Make sure your PR title starts with JIRA issue id, e.g., 'HADOOP-17799. Your PR title ...'.\n-->\n\n### Description of PR\nif there are two or more blocks exist in a same rack, it may cause unique data block is added to exactlyOne processing list when choosing redundancy stripted block to delete.\n`\n\n  storages.remove(cur);\n  if (storages.isEmpty()) {\n    rackMap.remove(rack);\n  }\n  if (moreThanOne.remove(cur)) {\n    if (storages.size() == 1) {\n      **\n\n      final DatanodeStorageInfo remaining = storages.get(0);\n      moreThanOne.remove(remaining);\n      exactlyOne.add(remaining);\n\n      **\n    }\n  } else {\n    exactlyOne.remove(cur);\n  }\n\n`\n\nIn this case, moreThanOne list may\
  \ not contain the remaining block. The remaining block shouldn’t be deleted, but it is added to exactlyOne list. And then it will be deleted.\n\n### How was this patch tested?\nThe testcase is that:(EC 6+3)\nblk_-xxx009 in rack /d1/r1\nblk_-xxx008 in rack /d1/r1\nblk_-xxx008 in rack /d1/r2\nblk_-xxx008 in rack /d1/r3\nblk_-xxx007 in rack /d1/r4\nblk_-xxx006 in rack /d2/r1\nblk_-xxx005 in rack /d2/r2\nblk_-xxx004 in rack /d2/r3\nblk_-xxx003 in rack /d2/r4\nblk_-xxx002 in rack /d2/r5\nblk_-xxx001 in rack /d2/r6\nAfter the FBR is triggered and redundant data blocks are added to invalidate list, blk_-xxx008 in rack /d1/r1 and blk_-xxx008 in rack /d1/r2 need to be deleted, blk_-xxx009 is HEALTHY.\n"
===== logeveryblock-info-level =====
title: HDFS-16658. Change logLevel from DEBUG to INFO if logEveryBlock is true
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  HDFS operators can enable per-block logging to diagnose replica handling, but when that mode is on the messages are still emitted at DEBUG and are easy to miss in normal production logging.


  ## Desired outcome

  When `logEveryBlock` is enabled, the related block-processing messages should be promoted to INFO so operators actually see the diagnostic stream they explicitly turned on. This should only affect the intentional per-block logging path, not the rest of the NameNode logging policy.


  ## Acceptance signals

  With `logEveryBlock` enabled, the per-block message should appear at INFO level instead of DEBUG. Without that setting, existing log volume and log levels should remain unchanged.

  '

===== federation-resource-profile-apis =====
title: YARN-11160. Support getResourceProfiles, getResourceProfile API's for Federation
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A federated YARN deployment should expose the same resource-profile discovery features as a single-cluster deployment, but the router still lacks support for those profile lookups.


  ## Desired outcome

  The router should support both `getResourceProfiles` and `getResourceProfile`, merging the participating subcluster responses into normal federation-level results and recording success, failure, and latency metrics for those APIs.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Federated clients can retrieve the full profile list and an individual named resource profile through the router, and router observability includes successful and failed handling for both calls.

  '
===== federation-signaltocontainer-support =====
title: YARN-10122. Support signalToContainer API for Federation.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  YARN federation already routes several application-management operations through the router, but container signaling is still missing from that federated experience.


  ## Desired outcome

  The router should accept and forward `signalToContainer` requests, reject malformed requests clearly, and record normal success, failure, and latency metrics for that operation.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A valid federated `signalToContainer` call reaches the owning subcluster and returns a response, invalid requests fail clearly, and router observability includes `signalToContainer` activity in its metrics.

  '
===== federation-proxy-failover =====
title: YARN-11237. Fix Bug while disabling proxy failover with Federation
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In federated YARN setups, disabling classic RM HA failover should not accidentally disable the separate federation failover path, but the proxy provider currently ties those decisions together too loosely.


  ## Desired outcome

  Failover handling should continue to work when federation failover is enabled, even if RM HA auto-failover is turned off. The decision point needs to respect the federation-specific setting so Router and federation-aware clients do not lose failover protection just because non-federated HA failover is disabled.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A configuration with `FEDERATION_ENABLED=true`, `FEDERATION_FAILOVER_ENABLED=true`, and `AUTO_FAILOVER_ENABLED=false` should still report failover as enabled for the federation-aware proxy path. Non-federated behavior should remain unchanged.

  '
===== federationclientinterceptor-failure-logging =====
title: YARN-11137. Improve log message in FederationClientInterceptor
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  YARN federation operators rely on router logs to tell them which application call failed against which subcluster.

  ## Desired outcome

  Failure logs in `FederationClientInterceptor` should include the right request identifiers and subcluster information so operators can diagnose submission and report-retrieval issues from the logs alone.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The emitted warning and error messages name the affected operation and subcluster instead of printing misleading or partially formatted text.

  '
===== reservation-home-subcluster =====
title: YARN-11235. Refactor Policy Code and Define getReservationHomeSubcluster
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Reservation placement in YARN federation follows the same policy family as application placement, but the router policy code had grown repetitive and made reservation routing harder to support consistently.


  ## Desired outcome

  This is internal policy refactoring: the shared router-policy layer should be cleaned up so reservation routing can use a first-class `getReservationHomeSubcluster` path while existing policy decisions for applications remain consistent. The goal is maintainable policy code and a clearer contract for reservation placement, not a change in externally visible routing semantics.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Router policy implementations should continue honoring blacklist and active-subcluster constraints while exposing reservation home-subcluster selection through the common policy facade. Existing application routing behavior and public policy names should stay compatible.

  '

### Description of PR
The source files for `hdfs_count`, `hdfs_mkdir` and `hdfs_rm` uses `getopt` for parsing the command line arguments. getopt is available only on Linux and thus, isn't cross platform. We need to replace getopt with `boost::program_options` to make these tools cross platform.

### How was this patch tested?
This PR was tested by running the above tools locally.

## hdfs_mkdir

Ran the tool to create a directory.

```bash
$ ./hdfs_mkdir /home/gautham/new-dir
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10280768/151838650-55a1fc41-8d4c-4d72-9a3b-563cfd37857d.png)

The tool is then run with\
4	  \ the `-p` option to exercise the creation of intermediate directories.

```bash
$ ./hdfs_mkdir -p /home/gautham/a/b/c
```

The trailing `a/b/c` directories are created under the path `/home/gautham`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10280768/151836730-3f228afc-720f-4518-be93-0e656cb6969a.png)

The tool is then run with the `-m` option with `700` as the mode. This turns all the permission bits on for user and turns off all the permission bits for group and other users.

```bash
$ ./hdfs_mkdir -p -m 700 /home/gautham/d/e/f
```

The trailing `d/e/f` directories are created under the path `/home/gautham` with the permission of `700`, even for the intermediate directories.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Serialized per-requirement commit ritual for parallel agents.
3	# usage: req-commit.sh <slug> <changed-path-1> [changed-path-2 ...]
4	set -e
5	cd /workspace
6	slug="$1"; shift
7	if [ -z "$slug" ] || [ "$#" -lt 1 ]; then
8	  echo "usage: req-commit.sh <slug> <path> [path...]" >&2
9	  exit 1
10	fi
11	lockdir=/tmp/hadoop-req-commit.lock
12	# clear a stale lock older than 15 minutes (crashed holder)
13	if [ -d "$lockdir" ]; then
14	  find "$lockdir" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +15 -exec rmdir {} \; 2>/dev/null || true
15	fi
16	tries=0
17	while ! mkdir "$lockdir" 2>/dev/null; do
18	  sleep 2
19	  tries=$((tries+1))
20	  if [ $tries -gt 450 ]; then
21	    find "$lockdir" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +5 -exec rmdir {} \; 2>/dev/null || true
22	    tries=0
23	  fi
24	done
25	trap 'rmdir "$lockdir" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
26	git reset -q
27	mkdir -p requirement_patches
28	git add -- "$@"
29	git diff --cached -- "$@" > "requirement_patches/${slug}.diff"
30	if [ ! -s "requirement_patches/${slug}.diff" ]; then
31	  echo "ERROR: empty diff for ${slug} — refusing to commit" >&2
32	  exit 1
33	fi
34	git add -- "requirement_patches/${slug}.diff"
35	git commit -q -m "impl: ${slug}"
36	echo "OK: committed impl: ${slug}"

title: 'HDFS-16655. OIV: print out erasure coding policy name in oiv Delimited output'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators reviewing fsimage data with the offline image viewer often need erasure-coding policy information in the delimited export so they can do capacity analysis and compliance review without a live cluster.


  ## Desired outcome

  When delimited OIV output is requested with `-ec`, the export should include an `ErasureCodingPolicy` column populated with the policy name for files or directories that have one while still producing valid output for entries without a policy.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Delimited OIV output generated with `-ec` clearly distinguishes erasure-coded content by policy name and keeps a consistent tabular shape for files, directories, and entries that have no erasure-coding policy.

  '

=== audit-log-remote-port ===
title: HDFS-16266. Add remote port information to HDFS audit log
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Security and operations teams use HDFS audit logs to trace client activity, but source IP alone is often not enough to identify the real caller behind shared hosts or proxies.


  ## Desired outcome

  Administrators should be able to enable `dfs.namenode.audit.log.with.remote.port` so audit records also carry the client port, exposed as `clientPort`, while leaving the current audit format unchanged when the option is off.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Direct RPC and JSP-initiated audit events include remote-port information only when that setting is enabled, giving operators more precise forensic detail without changing the default log format.

  '
=== java11-javadoc-reference ===
title: HDFS-16635.Fixed javadoc error in Java 11
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Developers generating HDFS API documentation under Java 11 should not have package-level Javadoc fail because a class reference is written in a form the newer toolchain rejects.


  ## Desired outcome

  The startup-progress package documentation should render cleanly on Java 11 while still describing the NameNode startup phases and steps accurately.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Java 11 Javadoc generation no longer trips over that package description, and readers still see the same startup-progress narrative without a broken reference.

  '
=== lifelinesender-negative-wait ===
title: HDFS-16623. Avoid IllegalArgumentException in LifelineSender
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A delayed DataNode can calculate a negative wait before its next lifeline, which then bubbles into scheduling code as an `IllegalArgumentException` even though the correct behavior is simply to send the lifeline immediately.


  ## Desired outcome

  Lifeline scheduling should tolerate overdue timestamps by clamping the next wait to a non-negative value instead of propagating an invalid negative delay.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When the computed lifeline deadline is already in the past, the DataNode keeps running and schedules the next lifeline without throwing an `IllegalArgumentException`.

  '

1	title: HDFS-16535. SlotReleaser should reuse the domain socket based on socket paths
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Short-circuit read clients can reuse a previously opened domain socket when they release shared-memory slots back to a DataNode, but that optimization breaks down on hosts running multiple DataNodes. In those setups, reusing a socket without checking which socket path it belongs to can send the release request to the wrong DataNode and create noisy slot-release failures.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Slot release should only reuse a cached domain socket when it matches the same DataNode socket path as the slot being released. Clients should still benefit from socket reuse when the path matches, but multi-DataNode hosts must route each release request back to the correct DataNode instead of cross-wiring the optimization.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Shared-memory slot release reuses an existing domain socket only for the matching socket path, multi-DataNode deployments no longer send release traffic to the wrong DataNode, the previous performance optimization remains available for the single-path case, and short-circuit slot release completes without the spurious failures caused by mismatched socket reuse.
16	
17	  '

1	title: HDFS-16332. Handle invalid token exception in sasl handshake
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  In secure HDFS deployments, a block token can expire during the SASL handshake even though the client could recover by fetching a fresh token and retrying. Users should not see a generic read failure for a case that is recoverable.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Teach the data transfer SASL handshake to preserve token-specific failure information so an expired access token is surfaced as an InvalidBlockTokenException rather than a generic I/O error. Clients should then be able to retry transparently and continue both sequential reads and positioned or byte-range reads.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  If the handshake fails because the access token expired, the client refreshes the token and the read succeeds on retry instead of aborting the file read with a generic handshake error.
16	
17	  '

######

######

######

    && yum install -y $(pkg-resolver/resolve.py centos:8)

####

####
RUN pkg-resolver/install-epel.sh centos:8

RUN dnf --enablerepo=powertools install -y \
    doxygen \
    snappy-devel \
    yasm

RUN dnf install -y \
    bouncycastle \
    gcc-toolset-9-gcc \
    gcc-toolset-9-gcc-c++ \
    libpmem-devel

# Set GCC 9 as the default C/C++ compiler
RUN echo "source /opt/rh/gcc-toolset-9/enable" >> /etc/bashrc
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "--login", "-c"]

######

# to find and use GCC 9 for compilation
######
ENV GCC_HOME "/opt/rh/gcc-toolset-9"
ENV CC "${GCC_HOME}/root/usr/bin/gcc"
ENV CXX "${GCC_HOME}/root/usr/bin/g++"
ENV MODULES_RUN_QUARANTINE "LD_LIBRARY_PATH LD_PRELOAD"
ENV MODULES_CMD "/usr/share/Modules/libexec/modulecmd.tcl"
ENV SHLVL 1

ENV MODULESHOME "/usr/share/Modules"

ENV PCP_DIR "${GCC_HOME}/root"
ENV MANPATH "${GCC_HOME}/root/usr/share/man::"
ENV PATH "${GCC_HOME}/root/usr/bin:/usr/share/Modules/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one

# This script is useful to perform basic sanity tests for the given
# Hadoop RC. It checks for the Checksum, Signature, Rat check,
# Build from source and building tarball from the source.

set -e -o pipefail

usage() {
  SCRIPT=$(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[@]}")

  cat << __EOF
hadoop-vote. A script for standard vote which verifies the following items
1. Checksum of sources and binaries
2. Signature of sources and binaries
3. Rat check
4. Built from source
5. Built tar from source

Usage: ${SCRIPT} -s | --source <url> [-k | --key <signature>] [-f | --keys-file-url <url>] [-o | --output-dir </path/to/use>] [-D property[=value]] [-P profiles]
       ${SCRIPT} -h | --help

  -h | --help                   Show this screen.
  -s | --source '<url>'         A URL pointing to the release candidate sources and binaries
                                e.g. https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/hadoop/hadoop-<version>RC0/
  -k | --key '<signature>'      A signature of the public key, e.g. 9AD2AE49
  -f | --keys-file-url '<url>'   the URL of the key file, default is
                                https://downloads.apache.org/hadoop/common/KEYS
  -o | --output-dir '</path>'   directory which has the stdout and stderr of each verification target
  -D |                          list of maven properties to set for the mvn invocations, e.g. <-D hbase.profile=2.0 -D skipTests> Defaults to unset
  -P |                          list of maven profiles to set for the build from source, e.g. <-P native -P yarn-ui>
__EOF
}

MVN_PROPERTIES=()
MVN_PROFILES=()

while ((${#})); do
  case "${1}" in
    -h | --help )
      usage; exit 0 ;;
    -s | --source )
      SOURCE_URL="${2}"; shift 2 ;;
    -k | --key )
      SIGNING_KEY="${2}"; shift 2 ;;
    -f | --keys-file-url )
      KEY_FILE_URL="${2}"; shift 2 ;;
    -o | --output-dir )
      OUTPUT_DIR="${2}"; shift 2 ;;
    -D )
      MVN_PROPERTIES+=("-D ${2}"); shift 2 ;;
    -P )
      MVN_PROFILES+=("-P ${2}"); shift 2 ;;
    * )
      usage >&2; exit 1             ;;
  esac
done

# Source url must be provided
if [ -z "${SOURCE_URL}" ]; then
  usage;
  exit 1
fi

cat << __EOF
Although This tool helps verifying Hadoop RC build and unit tests,
operator may still consider verifying the following manually:
1. Verify the API compatibility report
2. Integration/performance/benchmark tests
3. Object store specific Integration tests against an endpoint
4. Verify overall unit test stability from Jenkins builds or locally
5. Other concerns if any
__EOF

[[ "${SOURCE_URL}" != */ ]] && SOURCE_URL="${SOURCE_URL}/"
HADOOP_RC_VERSION=$(tr "/" "\n" <<< "${SOURCE_URL}" | tail -n2)
HADOOP_VERSION=$(echo "${HADOOP_RC_VERSION}" | sed -e 's/-RC[0-9]//g' | sed -e 's/hadoop-//g')
JAVA_VERSION=$(java -version 2>&1 | cut -f3 -d' ' | head -n1 | sed -e 's/"//g')
OUTPUT_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR:-$(pwd)}"

if [ ! -d "${OUTPUT_DIR}" ]; then
    echo "Output directory ${OUTPUT_DIR} does not exist, please create it before running this script."
    exit 1
fi

OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX="${OUTPUT_DIR}"/"${HADOOP_RC_VERSION}"

# default value for verification targets, 0 = failed
SIGNATURE_PASSED=0
CHECKSUM_PASSED=0
RAT_CHECK_PASSED=0
BUILD_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED=0
BUILD_TAR_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED=0

function download_and_import_keys() {
    KEY_FILE_URL="${KEY_FILE_URL:-https://downloads.apache.org/hadoop/common/KEYS}"
    echo "Obtain and import the publisher key(s) from ${KEY_FILE_URL}"
    # download the keys file into file KEYS
    wget -O KEYS "${KEY_FILE_URL}"
    gpg --import KEYS
    if [ -n "${SIGNING_KEY}" ]; then
        gpg --list-keys "${SIGNING_KEY}"
    fi
}

function download_release_candidate () {
    # get all files from release candidate repo
    wget -r -np -N -nH --cut-dirs 4 "${SOURCE_URL}"
}

function verify_signatures() {
    rm -f "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_verify_signatures
    for file in *.tar.gz; do
        gpg --verify "${file}".asc "${file}" 2>&1 | tee -a "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_verify_signatures && SIGNATURE_PASSED=1 || SIGNATURE_PASSED=0
    done
}

function verify_checksums() {
    rm -f "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_verify_checksums
    SHA_EXT=$(find . -name "*.sha*" | awk -F '.' '{ print $NF }' | head -n 1)
    for file in *.tar.gz; do
        sha512sum --tag "${file}" > "${file}"."${SHA_EXT}".tmp
        diff "${file}"."${SHA_EXT}".tmp "${file}"."${SHA_EXT}" 2>&1 | tee -a "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_verify_checksums && CHECKSUM_PASSED=1 || CHECKSUM_PASSED=0
        rm -f "${file}"."${SHA_EXT}".tmp
    done
}

function unzip_from_source() {
    tar -zxvf hadoop-"${HADOOP_VERSION}"-src.tar.gz
    cd hadoop-"${HADOOP_VERSION}"-src
}

function rat_test() {
    rm -f "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_rat_test
    mvn clean apache-rat:check "${MVN_PROPERTIES[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_rat_test && RAT_CHECK_PASSED=1
}

function build_from_source() {
    rm -f "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_build_from_source
    # No unit test run.
    mvn clean install "${MVN_PROPERTIES[@]}" -DskipTests "${MVN_PROFILES[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_build_from_source && BUILD_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED=1
}

function build_tar_from_source() {
    rm -f "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_build_tar_from_source
    # No unit test run.
    mvn clean package "${MVN_PROPERTIES[@]}" -Pdist -DskipTests -Dtar -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true 2>&1 | tee "${OUTPUT_PATH_PREFIX}"_build_tar_from_source && BUILD_TAR_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED=1
}

function execute() {
   ${1} || print_when_exit
}

function print_when_exit() {
  cat << __EOF
        * Signature: $( ((SIGNATURE_PASSED)) && echo "ok" || echo "failed" )
        * Checksum : $( ((CHECKSUM_PASSED)) && echo "ok" || echo "failed" )
        * Rat check (${JAVA_VERSION}): $( ((RAT_CHECK_PASSED)) && echo "ok" || echo "failed" )
         - mvn clean apache-rat:check ${MVN_PROPERTIES[@]}
        * Built from source (${JAVA_VERSION}): $( ((BUILD_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED)) && echo "ok" || echo "failed" )
         - mvn clean install ${MVN_PROPERTIES[@]} -DskipTests ${MVN_PROFILES[@]}
        * Built tar from source (${JAVA_VERSION}): $( ((BUILD_TAR_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED)) && echo "ok" || echo "failed" )
         - mvn clean package ${MVN_PROPERTIES[@]} -Pdist -DskipTests -Dtar -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true
__EOF
  if ((CHECKSUM_PASSED)) && ((SIGNATURE_PASSED)) && ((RAT_CHECK_PASSED)) && ((BUILD_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED)) && ((BUILD_TAR_FROM_SOURCE_PASSED)) ; then
    exit 0
  fi
  exit 1
}

pushd "${OUTPUT_DIR}"

download_and_import_keys
download_release_candidate

execute verify_signatures
execute verify_checksums
execute unzip_from_source
execute rat_test
execute build_from_source
execute build_tar_from_source

popd

print_when_exit

payload.resultSummary:
Both requirements are committed. Summary of the work:

- **tools-unguava-preconditions** — committed (`d19fcebe`, 95 files + diff artifact). HADOOP-18018: this tree uses shaded Guava (`org.apache.hadoop.thirdparty.com.google.common.base.Preconditions`). I verified every usage in hadoop-tools was only `checkArgument`/`checkNotNull`/`checkState` (155/103/27 call sites) — all present with identical signatures in Hadoop's own `org.apache.hadoop.util.Preconditions` (`hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/util/Preconditions.java`), and no non-`%s` format templates, so runtime contracts are preserved (both Guava templates and `String.format` accept `%s`). The change is a pure import swap (`org.apache.hadoop.thirdparty.com.google.common.base.Preconditions` → `org.apache.hadoop.util.Preconditions`, including the 28 static imports and one wildcard static import in `hadoop-aws/.../staging/StagingCommitter.java`), done in place to respect import ordering. No file had a conflicting existing `org.apache.hadoop.util.Preconditions` import. Verified 0 remaining Guava `Preconditions` references under `hadoop-tools`. Modules touched: hadoop-aliyun, hadoop-aws, hadoop-azure, hadoop-azure-datalake, hadoop-distcp, hadoop-dynamometer.

- **hadoop-tools-visiblefortesting** — committed (`17e69d2e`, 79 files + diff artifact). HADOOP-17962: swapped `import org.apache.hadoop.thirdparty.com.google.common.annotations.VisibleForTesting;` → `import org.apache.hadoop.classification.VisibleForTesting;` (Hadoop's own annotation in hadoop-annotations, already on every module's classpath). No collisions with pre-existing imports; verified 0 remaining Guava `VisibleForTesting` imports under `hadoop-tools`. Note: the "import-restriction build checks" in the acceptance signals have no import-control configuration in this tree (checkstyle config in `hadoop-build-tools` has no ImportControl module; poms have no such rule), so no build-config change was applicable — the annotation replacement itself is the complete change.

Not run: Maven builds (per constraints). Verification was by exhaustive grep (zero remaining Guava references), API signature comparison of the used `Preconditions` methods, and confirmation that both diffs are non-empty and committed via `/tmp/req-commit.sh`. Interleaved commits from other agents are present in the log; only my 95/79 listed files were staged per commit.

import re
files = ["hadoop-common-project/hadoop-auth/pom.xml","hadoop-common-project/hadoop-common/pom.xml","hadoop-common-project/hadoop-kms/pom.xml","hadoop-common-project/hadoop-nfs/pom.xml","hadoop-common-project/hadoop-registry/pom.xml","hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-client/pom.xml","hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-httpfs/pom.xml","hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-nfs/pom.xml","hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-rbf/pom.xml","hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/pom.xml"]
for f in files:
    lines = open(f).read().splitlines()
    # find banned-illegal-imports line
    idx = [i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if 'banned-illegal-imports' in l]
    assert len(idx)==1, (f, idx)
    i = idx[0]
    # find enclosing <plugin> ... </plugin>
    depth = 0; start = None
    for j in range(i, -1, -1):
        if re.match(r'\s*</plugin>\s*$', lines[j]): depth += 1
        elif re.match(r'\s*<plugin>\s*$', lines[j]):
            if depth == 0: start = j; break
            depth -= 1
    depth = 0; end = None
    for j in range(i, len(lines)):
        if re.match(r'\s*<plugin>\s*$', lines[j]): depth += 1
        elif re.match(r'\s*</plugin>\s*$', lines[j]):
            if depth == 0: end = j; break
            depth -= 1
    block = lines[start:end+1]
    has_enforcer = any('maven-enforcer-plugin' in l for l in block)
    n_exec = sum(1 for l in block if '<execution>' in l)
    print(f, "lines", start+1, "-", end+1, "enforcer:", has_enforcer, "executions:", n_exec, "len:", len(block))
EOF
